body.text: Run started 2026-11-17T20:57:56Z (authoritative status). Task understanding: pick 2–3 arbitrary-heading two-blade charger plugs from the right, actively reorient each with opposing fingers while preserving the demonstrated wrist style, place blades up on the left and maintain until 60 s. First 60 minutes are reserved for reconstruction and validation; simulation begins only after that deadline. No target rounds. I will separate video observations from inferred geometry and physics, and use deployment starts without narrowing headings.

Reconstruction camera calibration is weakly constrained by rounded charger corners: unconstrained PnP drifts to weak perspective; a broad MoGe-constrained fit gives f=1050 px and 6.22 px RMS. The supplied pure-rotation background-flow model accumulates 17.8 deg, potentially interpreting handheld translation as rotation. Testing a plane-constrained six-DOF camera fit to frame-0 background correspondences. Segmentation montage inspected: good visible body outlines; white metal blades partly excluded and black entirely hidden near first grasp. Occluded object rotation will remain uncertain/invalid rather than invented.

Dense-frame inspection refines the contact plan: white contact approximately frames 76–211, lift around 110, finger turn around 113–150, placement/release around 180–211; black contact 251–386, lift around 282–290, finger turn 315–333, release around 380. Exact boundaries have 2–4-frame uncertainty. Raw silhouette tracking drifts in depth and produces incorrect blade directions; testing support-constrained static-pose fits and manually feature-seeded tracking before hand fitting. These are reconstruction refinements, not a robot training simulation.

Reconstructed demo scene check: both initially resting chargers remain supported over a 2 s MuJoCo rollout; drift 0.0171 mm each, final translational speeds below 4e-13 m/s. Current visible-mask replay medians are 0.867 (white) and 0.869 (black), with measured hand masks as occluders. Initial and final blade directions visually reviewed. Exact occluded rotations remain inferred and receive broad uncertainty; entirely hidden frames invalid. Human hand fitting is underway using the unchanged mandated MANO fitter. These checks concern only reconstruction geometry.

Default MANO fit is insufficient despite 0.848 mask IoU: validator finds white thumb contact 0%, black opposed contact 31%, and finger self-intersection in 47.5% of visible frames. A nearest-probe contact loss is insufficient. I will retain this baseline with its failures, triangulate the Blender export so signed mesh checks are meaningful, and test a workspace copy of the fitter with explicit thumb-plus-opposing-finger contact and finger separation. Installed fitter code remains unchanged; all added terms and settings will be recorded.

body.text: The full reconstruction hour has elapsed; Stage 1 fitting is stopped. Selected reference is reconstruction version 7, r0014 (format VALID, supplied quality PASS, own support/motion audit corrected). Final review limitation: invalid black frames include segmentation/tracking failures on partially visible objects, not only full occlusions; the 81-frame count must not be read as 81 fully hidden frames. No unobserved pose is promoted to measured truth. Criteria now recorded before any robot simulation or policy evaluation. Proceed to construct the simulation, prove task feasibility, then teacher-data-BC-fine-tune under contract v3.

Physical grasp diagnostic: the first kinematic thumb/index profile drops the plug within0.2s. The inspected three-view montage shows separation before any intended turn. Closest-point geometry reveals the thumb contacting the upper rounded edge, with a largely downward normal, rather than two opposing side-face normals. Other-finger self-intersection is5.1mm. Tighten contact-centre/normal constraints and park unused fingers clear; then add current-limited preload using the actual response-matched gains, not constant gains. This is isolated primitive design, not a task-feasibility claim.

CPU evaluator prototype now uses native double-precision MuJoCo with policy events exactly every1/30s, controller events every.01s and physics events every1/1500s. Public default PoseSensor replay passes on a2s hold episode (60policy steps,391state rows). Own64-seed supported-start test passes64/64, with no stops and maximum measured palm change0.01degree. These are interface/start validations only; physical manipulation remains unproven. Frozen anatomical reference mapping is prepared from reconv7 before judging policies. Allocate the next2h to simulation/suite completion and a physically valid opposed grasp; then reassess the teacher strategy.

The opposing-contact probe initially supports body weight but rotates and loses its grip. The first model used condim3 point friction, which cannot transmit torsional torque about an antipodal pinch normal. The hardware has soft gloved pads. MuJoCo documentation explicitly recommends condim4 for soft fingers (https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/computation/index.html#condim). Test finite torsional friction with an unmeasured1–5mm effective contact-patch diameter (baseline3mm), randomized independently; no adhesion or rolling lock. This is a declared physical assumption requiring sensitivity tests, not a measured glove property. Keep object/table point contacts condim3.

Test asymmetric free-face spin prior: middle drives extension about upward-turn axis, thumb target only30% to permit contact rolling. Two final yaw choices0/+30, <=600s fit each. In parallel next distinct teacher method: direct CEM of smooth robot-joint gait residuals around best geometric prior, population64 times4physicsseeds, budget90generations/90min. Require physical opposed hold, net45deg finger elevation to75deg, activefraction>=.75/passive<=15, no hardware violations; geometry alone is not a pass. Current pure-PPO budgets are closed (r0070-72). No evaluator changes.

Directional kinematic audit: for blade initially along palm+Z (parallel to fingers), upward turning needs extension about world-Y; middle can do this but thumb axes have little available range. For blade opposite palm+Z, the needed turn changes sign and middle flexion may be easier. Current wrist-style heading adaptation already wraps pickup heading modulo pi (criteria2 source), so arbitrary deployment headings require both blade directions in essentially the same wrist pose. Test reverse-blade grasps explicitly (rotate object180deg about its horizontal support-face up axis, not local bladeZ). Two free-face/asymmetric-spin fits, whiteXup and blackXup, <=600s each. Opposing face normals must reverse to preserve initial physical contact sides. No hardware/criterion changes; opposite-direction grasp is a deployment adaptation, not a claim that canonical parallel grasp succeeds.
